newsitem.title: USA: Aspen extends Denverton Creek field.
newsitem.headline: Aspen extends Denverton Creek field.

text.p: Aspen Exploration Corp said the Emigh No. 34-1 well extended productive limits of the Denverton Creek field in Solano County, Calif., in a northeasterly direction.

Aspen said it holds a 12 percent working interest before payout and a 23.55 percent working interest after payout in this well, which was drilled to a depth of 10,200 feet and perforated one interval in the Bunker Formation.

It said natural gas sales started Nov 13, and after one week of production, the flow rate is about 3.3 million of high Btu natural gas, 18 barrels of condensate and 6 barrels of salt water per day. Current natural gas prices are $2.59 per million Btu, Aspen said.
Based on log analysis and mud log shows, it appears that about 70 to 100 feet of additional pay may exist behind-pipe in the Bunker and several other zones. These zones will be tested in the future.
Aspen said it has 960 acres under lease in the immediate vicinity and may drill a follow-up well in the spring of 1997.

It said the Denverton Creek Field has produced some 26 billion cubic feet of high Btu -- 1,045 to 1,070 Btu's per cubic foot -- natgas from the Bunker, McCormick, Martinez, Peterson, H&T, and 1st Starkey Sands.
